[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🪙Finances Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The finances module contains features related to the finances of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💵Collections", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z52PVRpfzT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A collection tracks donations from people for specific functions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hh6-W_FmMh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each time a collection is taken, a New Collection should be created. When creating a new collection note the following:
- Although not required, It is recommended to link the collection to the Function in which the collection is being taken.
    - By regularly linking functions to collections, it will be possible later to run reports to see collection amounts for specific function types, etc.
- Remember: After saving a collection, it will be in a draft state. In order to finalize the collection, you will need to 'Submit' the collection. Once submitted, it cannot be modified unless you cancel and amend it. Do not cancel and amend the collection of an online gift: cancelling it marks the gift Refunded, and Churchit does not let you amend it.
    - See the 'Terminology' section in the Help guide for more information about document states (draft / submitted / cancelled / amended / etc).
- After submitting the collection, you can click the Bank Reconciliation Report button on the top right of the form. This report can be used to compare with bank deposit reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kVjzsXy2-5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Finances workspace, contains links to view the collection list and various collection reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8K2QjgOLSb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🤲Donations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bZ3I5EEmVO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A donation tracks the amount given from a person toward a church fund. For tracking monies given to people in need, see Alms below.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HSRUNh_Fan", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding donations to a collection, note the following:
- After entering each donation, the collection total and fund totals will be updated in real-time.
- If a single donation check specifies multiple funds, enter it as two separate donations (one for each fund).
- Additional payment types can be added if needed.
- When entering a donation from a specific person (i.e. Check donation or Cash Envelope), it is highly recommended to link the donation to the person.
   - By regularly linking donations to persons, end-of-year statements and individual person donation reports can be created.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fin_r3_envelope", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Envelope numbers. A person can have an Envelope Number: the number on their offering envelopes or the reference on their bank gifts. When you enter a gift, type the envelope number in the Person field of the donation row to find the giver. Two people in one church cannot have the same number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fin_r3_noncash", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Non-cash gifts. When someone gives property, such as equipment or goods, and not money, add a donation row with the Payment Type Non-Cash. Type a description of what was given in Description, and keep the amount 0. Churchit does not let you save a non-cash row with an amount or without a description, because the church describes the gift and does not state its value. The giver's statement shows the description in place of an amount. Non-cash gifts do not change fund balances or collection totals. You can mark another Payment Type as Non-Cash on its form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z1nAaK7FS7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Finances workspace, contains links to view donation reports. ", "col": 12}}, {"id": "finDates1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The donation and expense reports count only submitted collections and expenses. A report or a giving statement for a date range includes all of its last day, so a gift at 11:59 PM on the last day counts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "givingDates1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Giving on the Person form. A gift counts toward a person's First Gift, Last Gift and Lapsed Giver when its collection is submitted. A draft or cancelled collection does not count. Lapsed Giver is ticked when the last gift was more than 90 days ago but within the last year. The Lapsed Givers list, under Collection Reports, shows these people with their first and last gift dates and when they last attended. A Church Manager can have it emailed to a finance user with ⋯ > Setup Auto Email. Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see these fields.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💳Online giving", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_setup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members and guests give online on the Give page. Churchit uses the payment gateways of the Payments app, and it works with two of them: Stripe and PayPal. To set up online giving:
1. A System Manager enters the account keys in Stripe Settings or PayPal Settings. Only a System Manager can see and change the gateway settings and keys.
2. Open Giving Settings. Add the gateway in Payment Gateways, mark one row as the default, and tick Enable Online Giving.
3. On each fund that people can give to, tick Allow giving to this fund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_limits", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Limits of the two gateways.
- Stripe cannot ask for 3-D Secure, the check in which the bank asks the card holder to confirm the payment. When a card needs 3-D Secure, the gift is declined. In the UK and in the EU many cards need it, so churches there use PayPal.
- PayPal Settings holds one PayPal account for the whole site, so every church that uses PayPal gets its gifts in that one account. Stripe can hold one account for each church: add one Stripe Settings record for each account.
- The payment page of each gateway shows the card fields in a frame inside a page of your site. Thus the PCI DSS 4.0 rules for scripts on payment pages apply to your site: keep a list of the scripts on these pages with the reason for each, and make sure that you find out when a script changes. Ask your payment processor what it needs from you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "givChurchGate1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online giving with more than one church. Each gateway row in Giving Settings has a Church. Name a church and that gateway serves only it, which is how each congregation's gifts reach its own account; leave it blank and every church can use it. A church with its own gateways uses only those. Wording Per Church does the same for the thank you message and the statement acknowledgment, so a branch's receipts carry its own words.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "givOnline1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online gifts. Online giving works with Stripe and PayPal. Giving Settings refuses a gateway of another kind, and the Give page does not offer one. When the gateway confirms a payment, Churchit compares the amount and the currency that the gateway charged with the Online Donation:
- When they agree, Churchit records the gift in a Collection and sets the status to Paid.
- When they do not agree, Churchit records nothing and sets the status to Needs Review. The Church Finance users of the gift's church get an alert that gives the charged amount and the gift amount. Check the payment in the gateway before you do anything else.
- When the gateway charged a gift but the gift stays Pending, for example because the confirmation did not arrive, the Church Finance users of its church get an alert each day. Open the gift and click Record Charged Gift. Churchit checks the payment again and records the gift one time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_fee_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Processing fees", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_fee", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A giver can add the processing fee to a gift, so that the church gets the full gift. Open Giving Settings. In the gateway row, tick Offer Fee Cover and type the card rate in Fee Percent and Fixed Fee, for example 2.9 and 0.30. Fee Percent must be less than 100, and neither field can be less than 0. The Give page then shows \"Cover the processing fee\" with the amount, worked out with the card rate. Churchit calculates the fee on the server from these two fields, so the giver cannot change it. The fee is part of the gift: the Online Donation shows it in Covered Fee, and the collection, the receipt and the giving statement show the full payment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_link_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give links and QR codes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_link", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open a fund that has Allow giving to this fund ticked and click Give Link. The dialog shows a QR code and the address of the Give page with this fund chosen.
- Click Download QR Code to get the code as an SVG file for a bulletin, a poster or a giving card.
- Click Copy Link to copy the address.
- To fill in an amount, add &amount=25 to the end of the address.
- To make a tap to give tag, write the address on an NFC tag with a phone app.
With more than one church, the address names the fund's church, and that church must be published.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_text_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Text-to-give", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_text", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With text-to-give, a person sends a text to a phone number and gets back a link to the Give page. Churchit does not receive texts, so your text provider sends this reply. Churchit does not log these texts, and they are not on any timeline. To set it up:
1. Get a separate phone number for giving from your text provider, for example Twilio. Do not use the number that sends your Church Emails and other texts, because the reply goes to every text that comes in.
2. Get the link. For the Give page, the link is your site address followed by /give, for example https://yourchurch.org/give. For one fund, click Give Link on the fund, then click Copy Link. This link looks like https://yourchurch.org/give?fund=FUND-0001. To fill in an amount, add &amount=25. With more than one church, the link also names the church, for example https://yourchurch.org/give?church=CHR-02&fund=FUND-0001.
3. Set the number to reply with the link to every text. A provider that has keyword replies can reply only to the texts that have the word GIVE. In Twilio, add a TwiML Bin with this text, and put your link in it: <Response><Message>Thank you for giving. Give here: https://yourchurch.org/give</Message></Response>. In the bin, write each & in the link as &, for example https://yourchurch.org/give?church=CHR-02&fund=FUND-0001. If you do not, Twilio does not accept the bin. Then open the phone number in Twilio. Under A message comes in, choose TwiML Bin and this bin, and save.
4. Send a text to the number from your own phone. Make sure that the link comes back and opens the Give page.
The text provider handles STOP replies to the giving number, as for all texts. The Communications manual tells how, in Text replies and STOP.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_other_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other ways to give", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_other", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Giving Settings and write your bank transfer, standing order or mailing details in Other Ways to Give. The Give page shows this text below the form, also when online giving is off. A church can have its own text: add a row for it in Wording Per Church and fill in Other Ways to Give. A church with no text of its own shows the site text.
A signed-in member who has an envelope number sees it on the Give page as the payment reference to use. Enter these gifts in a collection, and type the envelope number in the Person field of the donation row to find the giver.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_guest_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give a guest gift to a person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_guest", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A guest who gives without logging in has no person on the gift, so the gift is not on a giving statement. To find these gifts, click Gifts with No Person on the Finances workspace or in the sidebar. Open the Online Donation, set Person and save. The donation row of the gift's collection then names that person, with the person's email, and a comment on the collection says which gift changed. The next giving statement for that year includes the gift. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_refund_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record a refund", "col": 12}}, {"id": "onl_refund", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Refund the gift at the payment processor first. Churchit does not send the refund.
- For a full refund in the same year as the gift, open the gift's collection and cancel it. Churchit removes the gift from the fund balance and sets the Online Donation to Refunded. If the gateway confirms the payment again later, Churchit records nothing. You cannot amend the cancelled collection.
- If you already exported the dates of the gift to your accounting system, do not cancel the collection. Make a new collection with a negative donation row for the full amount, as for a partial refund. Thus the GL Journal shows the refund.
- For a partial refund, or a refund in a later year, make a new collection with the date of the refund. Add a donation row for the same person and fund with a negative amount, for example -20, and submit it. The giving statement for the year of the refund shows the lower total.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "reg_pay_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Event registrations and paid forms. A function sign-up or a form with a price takes an online payment through the gateways of the Give page. The Ministries manual tells how to set the prices. Each payment comes in as a submitted Collection with one row for the fund of the function or the Question Set, and no person, so it is not on a giving statement. It goes to the church of the function or the set, or to the church that shared it. When the gateway charged an amount that is not the amount due, or charged a record that is already paid, Churchit records nothing and alerts the Church Finance users of that church. Each day, Churchit also alerts them about sign-ups and form responses that a gateway charged but that are not recorded.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "reg_refund_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Registration payments by hand. For a sign-up paid in cash or by check, open the sign-up and click Payment, then Record Offline Payment. Churchit adds no Collection, so put the money in the weekly collection. When a payment arrives after a sign-up lost its seats, or when a paid sign-up is cancelled or declined, its Payment Status is Refund Due and Church Finance gets an alert. Refund it at the payment processor and cancel its Collection or add a negative donation row, as for a gift. Then click Payment, then Record Refund on the sign-up, or Record Refund on the Form Response. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧾Giving statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_make", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A giving statement lists a giver's gifts for a period, for the giver's tax records. In the Giving Statement list, click Generate Statements and enter From Date and To Date. Churchit makes or rebuilds the statements from the submitted collections in those dates.
- A statement shows only gifts to funds that have Tax Deductible ticked (see Funds below).
- A non-cash gift shows its description in place of an amount, and the total counts only money.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_email_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Email the statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stm_email", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the Giving Statement list, click Email Statements. Enter the same From Date and To Date that you used to generate the statements, then click Email. Churchit sends each statement to the giver's primary email at the time it sends, with the statement attached as a PDF. The emails go out in the background, so you can continue to work.
- A statement with no email address is not sent. Print it and mail it instead.
- A giver who unsubscribed from all email gets no statement email, and the statement is not marked as emailed.
- A statement that was emailed once is not sent again. If you generate the statements again and a gift on a statement changes, the next Email Statements sends the new statement. To send all of them again, tick \"Send again to statements already emailed\".
- Each email is written in the Access Log. To change the text of the email, edit the Email Template \"Giving Statement\".", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Pb91OTOhF1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Giving statements with more than one church. A statement is issued in your church, also for a giver from another church who gave at your collections. A giver who gave at two churches gets a statement from each. You cannot move a statement to a church that is not yours, or take one from another church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📥Import giving history", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_intro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can add past gifts from another church system, from a spreadsheet or from your payment processor. Churchit uses Frappe's Data Import tool. Data Import reads the file, shows a preview, and adds the gifts in the background. Church Finance users, Church Managers and System Managers can import gifts.
Each row of the file is one gift. Churchit adds each gift as a donation to a draft collection. The gifts of one batch on one date go in one collection, and its Expected Total is the sum of these gifts. Check each draft collection and submit it. The gifts count in the funds, the reports and the giving statements only after you submit the collection. Churchit does not send a thank you email for an imported collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_columns", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The file has these columns. You must fill in Gift ID, Date, Amount, Fund and Payment Type.
- 'Gift ID': the ID of the gift in the system it comes from, for example a Stripe charge ID. Churchit imports each gift one time.
- 'Date' and 'Amount': the date of the gift and the full amount that the giver paid.
- 'Fund' and 'Payment Type': a fund and a payment type of your church. A gift with the payment type Check also needs a 'Check Number'.
- 'Imported From' and 'Person ID': the system name and the ID of the giver from your People import. Leave 'Imported From' blank when you imported the people from a spreadsheet.
- 'Email': finds the giver when the Person ID does not. Only one person in your churches can have this email.
- 'Batch': the gifts of one batch and one date go in one collection. When you leave it blank, the batch is the name of the Data Import.
- 'Notes': text for the donation.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_steps", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the Finances sidebar, click Data Imports, then click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Giving Import. Keep Import Type as Insert New Records.
2. Save, and click Download Template to get the columns. You can also use the export of your payment processor (see below).
3. Upload the file and click Next. When the file has a column name that Churchit does not know, select the Churchit column that it agrees with, or do not import the column.
4. Look at the preview. A row that cannot be imported stops the import. Correct the file, or click Skip Row.
5. Click Import. Then open the Collection list, filter on Import Batch, check each draft collection and submit it.
If your church uses its own copy of the Donation Acknowledgment notification, set its Condition to doc.donations and not doc.import_batch before you submit imported collections. If you do not, each giver gets an email for each old gift.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_refusals", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The preview stops a row when:
- Churchit does not know its fund or payment type, or its fund belongs to another church.
- No person, or more than one person, has its Person ID or email.
- A donation already has its Gift ID. Thus a second import of the same file adds nothing. You can import the gift of a cancelled collection again.
- An earlier row of the file has the same Gift ID.
- Its payment type is a non-cash type, such as Non-Cash. Enter a non-cash gift in a collection with a description.
- An online donation that your payment processor charged has the same amount, date and email. This includes a Pending or Needs Review gift. Record that gift from the online donation, not from the import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gimp_stripe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import gifts from Stripe. Use this for gifts that givers make on the pages of Stripe, for example recurring gifts and bank debits. Churchit records the gifts from your Give page itself, so do not import them again.
1. In the Stripe Dashboard, open Payments, set the dates and click Export. Download the CSV file.
2. Open the file in a spreadsheet. Delete each row whose Description starts with \"Online gift to the\". These are the gifts from your Give page, which Churchit has already.
3. Delete each row whose Status is not Paid, and each row with an Amount Refunded.
4. Rename these columns: id to Gift ID, Created date (UTC) to Date, Customer Email to Email. Keep Amount. Delete the other columns.
5. Add the columns Fund and Payment Type, and fill in a fund and a payment type of your church on each row. You can add a Batch column, for example with the month.
6. Import the file with the steps above.
Stripe gives the date in UTC. A gift late in the evening can have the date of the next day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vVJ7g0tHHy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📊Funds", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4znr2XFUMc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Funds are used by churches to tag monies for a specific purpose. Some default funds are included (i.e. General, Building, Missions, etc), but additional funds can be created for your own purposes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "37szS6a0yE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding/managing a fund, note the following:
- Any collections that contained donations the the fund will be listed in the 'Transactions' section at the bottom of the fund form.
- The transactions of a collection take the date of the collection, not the day it was submitted.
- Manual transactions can created for the fund if needed
    - If the transaction is a transfer between funds, then create a fund transfer instead. Fund transfers automatically add a transaction to the fund.
    - If the transaction is documenting an church expense, add an expense instead. By choosing the expense type, an associated fund transaction will automatically be created. ", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fin_r3_deductible", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tax Deductible. Giving statements are tax receipts, so they show only gifts to funds that have Tax Deductible ticked. New funds have it ticked. Untick it for a fund whose gifts are not tax deductible, for example a collection that you pass on to another organization. A fund that is shared by all churches has one setting for every church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Tdfr6-sFUJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Finances workspace, contains links to view fund reports along with a graph showing the current totals in each fund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fundShared1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Funds with more than one church. A fund belongs to one church until you tick Shared with all churches on it, which every church can then give to and spend from: a joint building fund, or one missions fund the whole organisation supports. Sharing a fund shares the pot: its balance and its list of transactions are the joint ones, and every church that can see the fund can see them. Only the church that shared it can stop sharing it. Each gift and each expense still belongs to the congregation that gave or spent it, so every report shows a church only its own money. A fund transfer takes money out of a fund of your church or out of a shared fund. Only the church that owns a fund can move its money.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pledge_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🙏Pledges", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pledge_campaign", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Pledge Campaign is a giving campaign that people promise to support, such as a building campaign. Give it a title, the fund that receives its gifts, a start date, an end date and, if you want, a goal amount. Each campaign belongs to your church and is not shared with other churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pledge_pledge", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Pledge records what a person promises to give in total to a campaign. Set Family to make it a household pledge: the gifts of everyone in that household then count. Frequency records how often the giver plans to give. It does not change the pledged amount.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pledge_portal", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can pledge on the portal at /pledge. The page shows only the campaigns of their own church that have not ended. Everyone who uses the page pledges only for themselves, so the login must have a Person record. The list on the page shows only your own pledges. Staff add pledges for other people on the desk. A member cannot change a pledge after the campaign ends.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pledge_report", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Pledge Progress report shows each campaign with its goal, the total pledged and the total received, and then each pledge with the amount received from its giver. A gift counts when its collection is submitted, it goes to the campaign's fund, its collection belongs to the campaign's church, and its date is from the start date to the end of the end date. A gift at 11:30 PM on the end date counts. Expenses and fund transfers do not change the report. Enter each gift in a collection as usual.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1IhzkEsC60", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💸Expenses", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jgQMiK07Uh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expenses are any transaction that requires an outflow of funds. ", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wjAR7Nu3_S", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating an expense, note the following:
- An expense type must be chosen. If needed, you can create a new expense type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "67mC7yvAUx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expense Types", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fL3gBJn8g-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expense types are used to categorize different expenses. This allows for more fine-grained financial reporting.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WmN1sFvcpL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating an expense type, note the following:
- Each expense type is linked to a specific fund, so that when expenses of this type are created, a transaction for the related fund will also automatically be created.
- Expense types can be grouped in hierarchies. For example, you could have an expense type group of 'Waste' and then have sub-types of 'Trash' and 'Recycling'.
    - In the example above, the 'Waste' expense type would have the 'group' option checked and the 'Trash' and 'Recycling' expense types would have 'Waste' selected as the 'Parent Expense Type'.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "expTypeShared1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expense types with more than one church. Expense types are shared by every church, but the fund one names may not be. If a branch is told the fund belongs to another church, either tick Shared with all churches on that fund, or give the branch an expense type of its own pointing at a fund it can use.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hh7kswiBbD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🫴Alms", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tlzyc7xao2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Alms are monies given by the church to someone in need. For giving to the church, see Donations above.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wHgIFlrdYA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating an alms request, note the following:
- The Recipient is the person (or family) who would receive the alms
- With more than one church, the Requestor must be a person of your church. A request for a person of another church is made by that church.
- Once the alms request is Approved or Declined, the Status field should be updated.
- Once the alms have been distributed to the Recipient:
    - The Status can be set to Distributed.
    - An associated Expense can be created by clicking the Create Expense button at the top-right of the form. This will create and submit an Expense and automatically reduce the Fund associated with that Expense. Only a user who can edit the alms request can use the button. It makes one expense for each request, in the church of the request, and it is hidden when the request has an expense.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "alms_notify_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Emails. When someone adds an alms request, the Pastoral Care team and the Church Managers of its church get an email and a desk notification. To change it, open Notification and edit New Alms Request.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "alms_notes_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Case notes. On a saved alms request, click Case Notes. View Case Notes opens the notes about the person who gets the alms. Add Case Note adds a note in the Benevolence category. For a Family, the notes go on the primary contact of the family. Only the Pastoral Care team and the Church Managers can read and add Benevolence notes. The finance team does not see these buttons.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jbUyW5POXS", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "📊Budgets", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XKMT2w0u-K", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Budgets track expected expenses vs actual expenses over a given time period.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WkMLpIzenY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a budget, note the following:
- The total budget field will auto-update after adding new budget lines
- Each budget line consists of an expense type and an budgeted amount
- Notes can be added for each budget line
